scenario.title: Authorized recovery with post-intervention verification
scenario.attempted: After a bypassed 6-hour defrost, a routine command is attempted during the open incident; a corrective authority is revoked between commit and execution; a fresh authority restores the baseline; recovery is verified independently.

submissions.label: Routine defrost attempted during the open incident (current grant)
Corrective action: restore the authorized baseline

steps.detail: Independent EIN status FAULT; on-call technician and facility manager notified (simulated).
FM-01 issues a fresh, scoped corrective authority to TECH-01.
Routine defrost with a current grant: HOLD (MATERIAL_CHANGE_REQUIRES_REAUTHORIZATION, COMMIT_BOUNDARY_REFUSED)
FM-01 revokes the corrective authority after commit and before execution.
FM-01 issues a new corrective authority.
Controller restored from the sealed authorized configuration (assumes the attacker's access was also removed).

outcome: Baseline restored under fresh authority at minute 280. Simulated product peaked at -13.62 °C and spent 352 min above -18 °C; at the end it was -21.26 °C. Product disposition is not decided by TA-14.

claims.basis: CMD-S8-ROUTINE-DEFROST with a current grant: HOLD (MATERIAL_CHANGE_REQUIRES_REAUTHORIZATION, COMMIT_BOUNDARY_REFUSED)
Commit permitted: true; execution after revocation: DENY (AUTHORITY_REVOKED, EXECUTION_BOUNDARY_REFUSED)
CMD-S8-RESTORE-2 executed under ALLOW at minute 280 after revalidation.
Independent EIN first NORMAL after restore at minute 600; status at end NORMAL.
Chain valid: true (597 entries); sealed baseline unchanged: true; missing entry types: none.

unproven: Product disposition: TA-14 records the temperature excursion but does not decide food safety.
That restoring controller configuration removes an attacker's access (assumed here).
Physical-system behaviour: the thermal model is illustrative and unvalidated.
Real controller protocols, network paths and attacker capabilities were not tested.
Detection depends on independent sensors existing, being installed correctly and staying independent of the compromised path.
